insights.summary: Q2 FY27 was another record: revenue ₹2,542 Cr (up 144% year on year, 33% on the quarter), EBITDA ₹658 Cr at a 25.9% margin and PAT ₹394 Cr. The MD lifted FY27 revenue growth to at least 80% (from 40% in July and 20% in May) and said Q2 is not a peak. Order book is ₹28,900 Cr, with about 70% of the ₹18,500 Cr fibre and connectivity book from hyperscalers.

what_changed.text: FY27 revenue growth now at least 80% (July: 40%+, May: ~20%)
Defence revenue FY27 ₹500-600 Cr; FY28 at least ₹2,000 Cr; ₹5,000 Cr in 3 years
Fibre capacity target now 38 mn fkm, then 43; cable 39 to 63 mn fkm
Capex plan of about ₹1,800 Cr across fibre, cable and preform; own preform by Oct 2028
EPC profit now expected in Q1 FY28, not FY27; loss of ₹75-100 Cr more in H2

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: we do not see this quarter as a peak, but as the sustained phase of strong growth.

analyst_questions.answer: Analyst noted the guide implies flat or lower H2 versus Q2. MD: 'it is always good to be conservative'; no preform or capacity constraint.
Margins to get better, not worse, from connectivity mix, higher-spec fibre and own preform; no one-off in Q2.
₹28,900 Cr, delivered over up to 4-5 years, unevenly; ₹5,500 Cr of orders came in against ₹2,500 Cr supplied in the quarter.
Sees no slowdown; Europe, Asia and telcos should offset any weakness among debt-reliant data-centre builders.

red_flags.text: EPC lost about ₹121 Cr in Q2 because BharatNet milestone bills were not raised; profit pushed to Q1 FY28.
Fibre prices up about 20% this quarter; MD calls current preform prices 'insanity' and expects them to fall, which would also pull down fibre pricing.
Very high customer concentration: about 70% of the ₹18,500 Cr fibre and connectivity order book is hyperscalers, under NDA.
Own preform will cover only about half of fibre capacity and needs germanium that is not yet contracted.

watch_next: Q3 revenue above ₹2,542 Cr (MD said growth is certain)
EBITDA margin holding near or above 25.9%
Aerospace acquisition closing and defence revenue stepping up from ~₹80 Cr in H1
BSNL AMC signed; EPC loss within ₹75-100 Cr for H2

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Optical fibre and cables, data-centre connectivity, telecom equipment, defence products (thermal sights, fuzes, radars), EPC for telecom networks
business_snapshot.customers: Hyperscalers (about 70% of the export fibre book), Indian telcos, BharatNet/BSNL, Indian Army
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: Telecom about ₹2,300 Cr in Q2, of which data centres 65-75% and telcos 25-35%; defence about ₹80 Cr in H1
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: AI data-centre build-out in the US, telcos restarting fibre purchases, defence indigenisation
